ideal: Nxb4 allows Qxf7+ Kh8 Qxh7#, while Qxg5 removes the knight supporting the mate.
note: Both best-line claims are true, but allowing mate on h7 is the overriding error.

ideal: Qh3 allows the king-rook fork Nxc2+ Kd1 Nxa1, losing the a1-rook and c2-pawn.
note: The checking fork wins the rook; losing castling is a secondary consequence.

ideal: Bxb4 allows Qxb4+ Qd2 Nc2+, followed by Nxa1, losing the exchange when Rxa1 recovers the knight.
note: The rook-for-knight loss matters; castling rights matter little after the forced queen exchange.

ideal: Rd2 misses Rxf2, threatening Qxh2# against the exposed king.
note: The f2-pawn is real, but the mating attack is the main point of Rxf2.

ideal: fxe4 loses the g5-bishop to hxg5, which also threatens Qxh7#.
note: The bishop falls immediately, and the independent mate threat keeps the attack forcing.

ideal: c6 allows d6 Ng6 Qb3 Bxd6 Bxg8, losing the g8-knight for the d-pawn.
note: Qf7# is a genuine threat, but the knight lost on g8 is the main concrete damage.

ideal: Bg5 allows Bxf2+ Kxf2 Ng4+ Ke1 Qxg5, recovering the bishop while leaving your king unable to castle.
note: The checking sacrifice displaces the king, and Ng4+ wins back the bishop to leave Black a pawn ahead.

ideal: O-O-O allows Qa5, threatening Qxc7# against your newly castled king.
note: The a7-pawn falls, but Rc8 also concedes a pawn; the attack on the castled king distinguishes the error.

ideal: h3 allows Bc3 to threaten Rxe1#, leaving the e1-knight to fall after Ke2.
note: Bc3 protects e1 and creates a mating threat; the pinned knight cannot escape the rook.

ideal: Nxc6 misses Qf3, whose Qxf7# threat induces Qe7 before Nxc6 wins a pawn with tempo.
note: Qf3 makes the pawn capture come with an attack on the queen; immediate Nxc6 instead allows Qf6 and Qxc6.

ideal: Na7 misses Nxc7+ Kf7 Nxe6 Kxe6 Bxa6, winning a bishop and two pawns for a knight after dxe3 dxe3.
note: The material count is correct; depriving the king of castling is incidental in this queenless position.

ideal: Nd5 misses Bxg2, winning the g2-pawn after Qh4+ starts the queen exchange.
note: The later exchanges cancel the minor pieces, leaving a pawn gain; castling loss is incidental after queens come off.

ideal: a3 misses Qxe7 and instead loses the exchange after Bf6 Rxf6 gxf6.
note: Qe1# becomes a real threat once the f2-rook is sacrificed, but h3 answers it; the exchange loss is concrete.

ideal: Qf3 misses Nc4 and Bxg6+ hxg6 Qxg6+, winning the h-pawn while driving the king to d8.
note: The bishop trades cancel, leaving a pawn gain and an exposed king with queens still present.

ideal: Bd5 allows Qg5, threatening Qxg7# and winning the d5-bishop after Qxf6 Qxd5.
note: The mate threat explains why Black removes the f6-pawn instead of saving the bishop.

ideal: Nd1 allows axb4 Rhg1 Bd4+ Kc1 Rxa3, threatening Ra1#.
note: The material card needs Qxa3 and Qxh2 beyond the supplied line; the Ra1# threat is verified.

ideal: g4 allows fxe4 dxe4 Bh4, pinning f2 and letting Nxe4 win the e4-pawn.
note: The e4-pawn is genuinely lost; the later loss of castling is part of a longer attack rather than the immediate mechanism.

ideal: Rf1 allows Bh3, threatening Qxf1# and winning the exchange after Qe2 Qxf1+ Qxf1 Bxf1 Kxf1.
note: The mating threat forces a concession, and the queen exchanges leave a rook traded for a bishop.

ideal: fxe5 misses Bb5+ Nc6 Qxh5, winning the h5-bishop outright.
note: The mate threat on f7 is real, but winning the bishop is already a sufficient reason.

ideal: Bb2 allows Nxe4 dxe4 Qh4+ Ng3 Qxg3+ Ke2, driving your king into the open.
note: The knights exchanged on e4 and g3 cancel, leaving a pawn loss and a sustained attack on the displaced king.

ideal: Nd5 misses Nxb4, taking the b4-pawn with the threat of Nd3#.
note: The pawn capture and immediate mating threat are both real; the pawn is not won by that threat.

ideal: exd5 allows Bb5+ Nc6 Qxh5, losing the h5-bishop for the d5-pawn.
note: The material count includes the pawn captured by exd5; Qxf7# is an additional threat after Qxh5.

ideal: Qh5 allows Ne6, threatening Qxg7# while uncovering the bishop attack on the b8-rook.
note: The mate threat diverts Black from the rook; after the bishop trades cancel, Black loses a rook for a knight and pawn.

ideal: Nh7 allows Bxf7+ Kh8 Qg6; after Nf6 stops mate on g7, Bxe8 wins the rook.
note: The mate threats Qxg7# and Bxg7# force attention away from the e8-rook.

ideal: Ng5 abandons the e5-pawn, allowing Qxd1+ Kxd1 Nxe5.
note: Ng5 removes the pawn defender; losing castling after the queen exchange is secondary.

ideal: Qe2 allows Rf2, threatening Qxg2# and setting up Rxg2+ Qxg2 Qxe1+.
note: The mate threat leads to a checking deflection; the pawn-only card omits the later queen-for-rook loss.

ideal: Rg8 allows Qf4, threatening Qxh6# and winning the d4-bishop after Rg6 Rxg6 fxg6 Qxd4.
note: The bishop-for-pawn count requires the later Nxe5; the mate threat explains the defensive rook maneuver.

ideal: Bxe6 misses Qe4, threatening Qh1# and allowing Qd4+ before taking the e6-bishop.
note: The immediate bishop capture permits f5 and its eventual recovery; the mating threat supplies the useful tempo first.

ideal: Qg5 misses Qh4 and its immediate Qxf2# threat.
note: Both Qh4 and Qf6 threaten Qxf2#; the pawn gain alone does not explain the advantage over Qg5, which also wins pawns.

ideal: Rdg1 misses Rd6+ Kf5 Rgxg6, winning the g6-knight before Rf8 Rxc6 takes a pawn.
note: The d6-rook protects g6, and the Rdf6# threat draws Rf8 before the c6-pawn falls.
